data.description: The unlock: CFP-10 (w2) direct; makes the whole ABS-S3 scenario gradeable (~19 of 28 item-weight, area weight 20) and ABS-05 (w3) winnable. Build IN ORDER: (1) 'Invite reviewer' on the committee card doing all four writes transactionally (people -> memberships role=reviewer [NO runtime API for memberships exists today — you are creating the first] -> committee_members -> reviewer_track_scopes), returning a copyable magic link on demo conferences via existing mintMagicLink purpose=login redirectTo=/reviewer. (2) Demo door: add reviewer to roleSchema + DEMO_ROLE_TO_MEMBERSHIP (auth.routes.ts:32,319) AND fix the persona query (auth.routes.ts:98-105, no ORDER BY; seeded staffer holds owner+program_lead+reviewer — naive fix signs the judge in AS THE ORGANIZER, an outright CFP-10 fail). Exclude staff-role holders, add ORDER BY. (3) Landing third door LAST. Also relax evaluation.routes.ts:577 (reviewer-add requires pre-existing membership). Do NOT touch seat.tsx (already correct). Traps and full AC: section T-A of sequence/eval-response-tickets.md. Register rows 1-3.
data.title: Reviewer provisioning end to end

data.body:
PR open: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/82 (HEAD 0bf998a).

Local gate: npm run pr-gate -- --ticket MRQ-107 => {"command":"pr-gate","ticket":"MRQ-107","status":"pass","elapsedMs":59817,"budgetMs":120000}

Shipped, in the ticket's order: (1) POST /events/{id}/committees/{id}/invites — the four provisioning writes plus the audit row in one batch, then the existing mintMagicLink(purpose=login, redirectTo=/reviewer), returned on screen only on demo conferences; (2) addCommitteeReviewer relaxed to grant the missing reviewer membership instead of 404ing; (3) demo reviewer door with the persona-query trap closed (staff exclusion + deterministic ORDER BY) — verified live that role=reviewer resolves to Dario Quill, not the staffer; (4) landing third door last; (5) the invite dialog on the committee card. seat.tsx untouched.

Validation (artifact attached): live Worker on the shipped seed, organizer UI driven in the browser, then the invited reviewer's own seat via the link the dialog issued — 302 /reviewer, queue = 19 items scoped to Security out of the committee's 100 assignments, organizer register 403. Toggle measurement for the elements-never-jump rule: footer 736 -> 736.

Deviate-with-flag, three items:
1. TWO CONTRACT REGISTRIES AMENDED. tests/node/auth-boundary.test.mjs enumerates every mintMagicLink issuer (A-5); the reviewer invitation is a third. Enumerated with the argument in-file (the ticket's own instruction is to reuse mintMagicLink rather than invent a second credential path) plus two new assertions pinning the staff refusal and the login/redirect shape. tests/node/bulk-paths.AC-66-69.test.mjs: the two findDemoPersona expansions classified, replaceReviewerScopes renamed to its extracted owner ownedTrackIds. Neither was loosened. If either registry is meant to be immutable, this is the line to challenge.
2. LIVE-SMOKE DEFECT the tests missed: invited people were written is_demo=1, so the newest invitation captured the demo reviewer door (seeded rows carry a frozen future created_at and sort after a runtime row). An organizer inviting into a quiet track would have pointed the public reviewer door at an empty queue — the exact cannot_judge -> fail conversion T-A warns about. Fixed to is_demo=0, matching every other runtime person writer; pinned by a test.
3. STANDING EXPOSURE, not introduced here: on a demo conference an organizer can aim an invitation at any existing non-staff address and read back a link into that person's seat. The shipped public /api/v1/auth/magic-link already returns an on-screen link for any demo-event address to an ANONYMOUS caller, so this route sits at a strictly higher bar (program_lead). Worth a ticket across both routes.

Also removed a pre-existing lie: the committee card's 'View all N reviewers ->' opened a dialog with only a name field, and the card already listed every member. It is now the invite control.

Reviews: lattice's auto-fired review timed out at 600s under load 118 (COMMON fallback). Three headless rounds spawned directly instead: PASS-WITH-NITS (20dffe9) -> FAIL, two red contract registries (4209a2c) -> PASS-WITH-NITS (b721670) -> all nits fixed at 0bf998a. Full triage in the review artifact.

Merge-queue hold: captain owns merge order (#82 is 7th of 9). Branch rebased locally onto github/main 2fd9712, clean; NOT pushed. Remote still 4602ace. At my turn: rebase, regenerate cli/api-registry.json (generated file, taken from upstream through both rebases — check:api fails without the inviteCommitteeReviewer row), npm ci, pr-gate, force-push, confirm fast-gate. Local gate currently red on time only (run-test: pass-over-budget, 118s vs 45s budget, load 60-96); tests pass.

Suite-speed question settled: run-test at load 6.61 (16 cores) => status pass, 27488ms of a 45000ms budget, hermetic. The earlier 118s over-budget reading was contention at load 60-96, not a slow suite. No defect. Still holding for the merge captain; branch unchanged locally (rebased onto 2fd9712), remote #82 still 4602ace.

Rebased and pushed at merge-captain's turn call. Head dcf5a87, based on github/main 0f3ba05, clean rebase. API registry regenerated (141 ops, inviteCommitteeReviewer present). Local gate pass 31.5s/120s at load 8.62. PR #82: mergeable MERGEABLE, state CLEAN, fast-gate SUCCESS (run 31605955806) — CI had never fired before because a CONFLICTING PR has no merge ref for GitHub to build, so the pull_request workflow could not dispatch; it fired by itself once the rebase landed. PR body now carries the is_demo=1 finding as its own section. Awaiting Merge Warden; not merging, not deploying.

Merged by the merge captain as af7d0e5 (PR #82, head dcf5a87, fast-gate SUCCESS). Leaving status at pr_open per COMMON — done is the orchestrator's transition, not mine. Standing down. Two follow-ups I raised and am NOT carrying further, for whoever picks them up: (1) on a demo conference an organizer can aim a reviewer invitation at any existing non-staff address and read back a working sign-in link into that person's seat — the shipped public /api/v1/auth/magic-link already does this for an anonymous caller on any demo-event address, so the exposure predates this PR and wants closing across both routes; (2) unguarded people INSERT in the invite batch 500s rather than 201s if two simultaneous invites race the same new address — uq_people_org_email holds the invariant, so it is a UX wart, not corruption.

Board reconciliation 2026-08-12: verified DONE. PR #77 (mrq-127-create-pickers) merged 2026-08-12T08:21:37Z; merge commit 514f9f48 confirmed an ancestor of github/main via 'git merge-base --is-ancestor'. Ticket had drifted at pr_open. The repo has zero open and zero closed-unmerged PRs, so no work is waiting on review. Status corrected to reflect merge, not PR-open.

CORRECTION to the board-reconciliation review comment above: it cites PR #77, which is wrong — that is MRQ-127's PR. A shell loop consumed stdin and mispaired the ticket with the last entry in its mapping. MRQ-107's real PR is #82 (mrq-107-reviewer-provisioning), merged 2026-08-12T14:20:44Z, merge commit af7d0e55, re-verified as an ancestor of github/main. The delegator's own 14:22:21Z comment says the same. The 'done' status is correct; only the PR citation was wrong.
